findings.title: v4 pins the exact bytes of the frozen Claude v3 verdict and then misreports their contents, recording shouldFix as empty when that verdict carries one SHOULD-FIX, CLAUDE-V3-S-1 - the finding that caused the v3 REJECT.
measured: v4 records appliesFindingsOf.claude2v3 with sha256 3e092ad2b283a77936167fc451d5de605fbf75d8779eb73569f418bbd5c0243c. I re-hashed that file: the digest is correct.
The file at that digest records verdict REJECT, counts {blockers: 0, shouldFix: 1, advisories: 5}, and findings [{id: CLAUDE-V3-S-1, severity: SHOULD-FIX}].

v4 records for the same file: blockers [], shouldFix [], advisories [CLAUDE-V3-A-1..A-5]. The blockers and advisories transcriptions are correct. shouldFix is not: CLAUDE-V3-S-1 is absent from it and from every other list in the artifact.

idCollisionNote recharacterises it as 'Claude v3 used CLAUDE-V3-A-1..5 (0 blockers; previewScope residue in verdictBasis)' - describing a formally identified SHOULD-FIX finding as informal residue in a prose field. The finding was not in verdictBasis; it was in findings[0], with an ID and a severity.
notFoldedThisSuccessor books CLAUDE-V3-A-4 and CLAUDE-V3-A-5 but never books or names CLAUDE-V3-S-1.
honestyRepairsFromV3's closing line likewise calls it 'Claude v3 verdictBasis previewScope residue'.
findings.whyItIsABlocker: appliesFindingsOf is the machine-readable succession record, and the D-000 cycle turns on exactly these counts - adoption entries record 'CONSENT from both independent reviewers, 0 MUST-FIX, 0 SHOULD-FIX', and every review in this chain is bounded by 'ACCEPT only at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX'. A successor that reports a prior reviewer's SHOULD-FIX count as zero corrupts the input to that test, and does so while pinning the bytes that refute it. A coordinator auditing from v4's succession record would conclude the Claude v3 review reached 0/0 and that its REJECT rested on advisories alone; it did not. This is the mirror of the defect I blocked at v2, where the artifact claimed a finding folded that had not been - here the severity is erased instead of the fold. It is a record-integrity defect, not a design defect: the underlying issue is genuinely repaired, and the artifact does acknowledge and fix it under the 'residue' label in two places. That mitigation is why I state it plainly rather than compounding it, but it does not make the recorded count true.
findings.whatWouldClearIt: Set appliesFindingsOf.claude2v3.shouldFix to ['CLAUDE-V3-S-1'], correct idCollisionNote to name it as a SHOULD-FIX finding rather than verdictBasis residue, and relabel the honestyRepairsFromV3 line to 'CLAUDE-V3-S-1'. The repair text itself needs no change - only the record of what was repaired.

verdictBasis: ACCEPT was available only at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. Measured: 1 blocker, 0 SHOULD-FIX. Every design attack in the standing set is refuted and every one of my five v3 advisories is either repaired or explicitly booked as declined. The AL-3 split is not just claimed but verifiable against the D-107-accepted contract's own generation-versus-self-update boundary, and the uncovered AL-1/AL-2/AL-5 cases are honestly parked at DR-127 rather than blanket-routed to condition 4. On design, this version is sound. It fails on record integrity: v4 pins the frozen Claude v3 verdict by digest and then reports its shouldFix list as empty when that file records one SHOULD-FIX, CLAUDE-V3-S-1 - the finding that produced the v3 REJECT. The fix is to the record, not to the contract.

The AL-3 core-rollback fallback is conservative and correct - DR-110 is D-002-deferred with no accepted contract, so the obligation parks at DR-127 instead of being deferred.
